title: Stochastic and Dynamic Vehicle Routing in the Euclidean Plane: The Multiple-Server, Capacitated Vehicle Case. 1990
contribution: 1990 working-paper version of S032: extends the dynamic traveling repairman problem from one vehicle to m vehicles (heavy-traffic system time reduced by a factor 1/m^2, region-partition policies) and, per the title, to capacitated vehicles (abstract; the record's abstract is cut off).
problem_entry: {SD AP} Extends the authors' own DTRP (a constant-speed vehicle in a Euclidean region serving demands with stochastic arrival times, locations and on-site service, minimizing expected system time) to multiple, capacitated vehicles (abstract; title).
key_idea: New bounds and policies for m identical uncapacitated vehicles; heavy-traffic system time falls by a factor 1/m^2 against one server; policies divide the region into m equal subregions (abstract).
assumptions: Euclidean region, constant velocity, stochastic arrivals, locations and on-site service, infinite horizon; m identical vehicles with unlimited capacity in the first extension (abstract).
proof_devices: lower bounds on the optimal system time with light- and heavy-traffic policies within a constant factor (abstract, recapping the predecessor and extended to m vehicles)
positioning: Working paper OR 224-90 (August 1990; DSpace hdl 1721.1/5220) of S032 (Operations Research 41(1), 1993); the homepage lists this title as Operations Research 1993. The predecessor is, by its description, the DTRP paper S016 (OR 1991; working paper S261), inferred (metadata).
writing: The abstract recaps the predecessor's results at length before 'In this paper, we extend these results in several directions' (abstract).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Bounds on the optimal system time, an optimal light-traffic policy and constant-factor heavy-traffic policies (recapped), with new bounds and policies for m vehicles; compare card S016.

quotes.text: In this paper, we extend these results in several directions.

First, we propose new bounds and policies for the problem of m identical vehicles with unlimited capacity and show that in heavy traffic the system time is reduced by a factor of 1/m2 over the single server case.

title: Signed Budget Uncertainty for Robust Mixed-Integer Optimization
contribution: Signed and laminar budget uncertainty for robust MIO: compact robust counterparts whose size does not grow with the number of uncertain coefficients, a 2^K-nominal-problem method for one uncertain constraint, and solutions the classical budget parameter cannot reach (abstract).
problem_entry: {RO IO} Classical budget uncertainty bounds aggregate absolute deviations, but in many applications the information concerns aggregate signed deviations (abstract).
key_idea: Bound signed aggregates. With binary uncertainty-affected variables the robust counterpart needs two extra variables and two extra constraints per uncertain constraint, independent of the number of coefficients; laminar signed budgets encode hierarchical information with a counterpart that scales with the number of aggregate sets (abstract).
assumptions: Robust MIO with binary uncertainty-affected variables for the compact counterpart; laminar families of aggregate sets; a single uncertainty-affected constraint for the 2^K result (abstract).
proof_devices: compact robust counterpart: two extra variables and two extra constraints per uncertainty-affected constraint (abstract)
reduction to 2^K nominal problems for one uncertainty-affected constraint (abstract)
experiments: Experiments show computational advantages and solutions not obtainable by adjusting the classical budget parameter; instances not named in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Optimization Online, posted 2026-09-30; the newest work on the budget sets that S001 introduced; from the de Moor-den Hertog group of S377 and S708 (metadata).
writing: A contrast sentence against the standard counterpart's linear growth; the closing sentence claims solutions unreachable by the classical knob (abstract).
limits_future: The 2^K route covers a single uncertain constraint; the compact counterpart assumes binary uncertainty-affected variables (abstract).

method_links.note: A class-keeping device: a compact counterpart, and for one constraint a reduction to nominal solves (compare the n + 1 nominal solves of Method 1 step 3).
The lever is the set's shape (signed, laminar budgets), not the level of Gamma; the abstract argues that tuning the classical knob cannot reach these solutions.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: practitioners' maxims encoded as uncertainty-set geometry
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The information held (signed aggregates over a geographical, organizational or categorical hierarchy) becomes signed and laminar budgets; compare card S027.

transferable: If your information comes as net totals by region or category, encode it as signed, nested budgets; then show that the counterpart's size does not grow with the number of uncertain coefficients, and that the new set yields a solution no setting of the classical Gamma yields (abstract).
coauthors: Danique de Moor, Dick den Hertog, Federica Donnini

quotes.text: In many applications, however, information concerns aggregate signed deviations.
Experiments demonstrate the computational advantages and show that signed budget uncertainty can produce solutions not obtainable by adjusting the classical budget parameter.

title: A Robust Optimization Approach to Supply Chains and Revenue Management
contribution: A. Thiele's 2004 MIT PhD thesis, supervised by Bertsimas: budgeted polyhedral robust optimization for supply chains (robust equals deterministic with modified parameters) and a trimmed-sample, estimation-free robust approach for revenue management (thesis abstract).
problem_entry: {RO AP} Supply-chain and revenue-management problems under uncertainty need a tractable framework that shows the structure of the optimal policy and needs little knowledge of the distributions (abstract).
key_idea: (i) Polyhedral uncertainty sets with budgets of uncertainty trading robustness against optimality; for supply chains the robust problem equals a deterministic problem with modified parameters. (ii) Historical realizations used without estimation: remove a fraction of the best cases and optimize the sample average of the rest; for revenue management the optimal policy often ranks the historical data (abstract).
assumptions: Polyhedral sets with budgets; for the second approach only historical realizations, no estimated distribution (abstract).
proof_devices: robust problem shown equivalent to a deterministic problem with modified parameters (abstract)
positioning: Student thesis (DSpace hdl 1721.1/16693; MIT EECS PhD 2004; advisor Bertsimas) that Scholar credits to him; the corpus holds four Bertsimas-Thiele papers: S055, S014, S027 and S122 (metadata).
writing: Thesis abstract opens with 'The contribution of this thesis is ...' (abstract).

method_links.note: Budgets of uncertainty set as a robustness-optimality trade-off (the student's text, evidence for his programme).
The robust problem equals a deterministic one with modified parameters, so the nominal structure carries over.
A 2004 thesis he supervised inside the robust-optimization programme, with four joint papers in the corpus.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Thesis abstract: the robust supply-chain problem is equivalent to a deterministic problem with modified parameters; the device of the S014 and S027 cards.

coauthors: author Aurélie Thiele; advisor Dimitris J. Bertsimas

quotes.text: The polyhedron is affected by budgets of uncertainty, which reflect a trade-off between robustness and optimality.

We apply this framework to supply chain management, show that the robust problem is equivalent to a deterministic problem with modified parameters, and derive the main properties of the optimal policy.

title: Distributionally Robust Optimization with General Uncertainty Structure
contribution: An exact framework for DRO with general uncertainty structure: a weakly nested ambiguity set built from linear confidence sets, and three cases solved by reformulating DRO as a robust problem (a global algorithm, or an explicit conic reformulation) (abstract).
problem_entry: {RO CP} Exact methods for DRO with moment- and confidence-set-based ambiguity sets are largely limited to max-of-affine functions under strictly nested confidence sets (abstract).
key_idea: Introduce an ambiguity set from linearly defined confidence sets that allows weak nestedness; for functions convex in the decisions: convex in the uncertainty, a global optimization algorithm; generally nonlinear, the same algorithm under the new set; concave, an explicit conic reformulation; all via a robust reformulation of the DRO problem (abstract).
assumptions: Moment- and confidence-set-based ambiguity sets; nested or weakly nested (linear) confidence sets; functions convex in the decision variables (abstract).
proof_devices: reformulation of the DRO problem as a robust problem (abstract)
global optimization algorithm for the convex case (abstract)
explicit conic reformulation for the concave case (abstract)
experiments: Two applications: capital budgeting and appointment scheduling (abstract).
positioning: Optimization Online, posted 2026-06-11; den Hertog's line of exact reformulations carried into DRO (tags: reformulation-perspectification techniques, cutting-set methods; compare S708) (metadata).
writing: The three cases are enumerated (i)-(iii) in one sentence (abstract).
limits_future: Cases (ii) and (iii) need the alternative ambiguity set (abstract).

method_links.note: DRO rewritten exactly as a robust problem, with a conic reformulation in the concave case; the ambiguity set is changed so that tractability is preserved.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: exact optimum on a small solvable instance as the certificate for a heuristic
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Variant: exact DRO optima serve as the yardstick for the conservatism of approximation-based DRO models; instance size not stated.

transferable: When exact methods depend on a structural assumption (strict nesting), redefine the ambiguity set so that a weaker version suffices, then sort the functions by their convexity in the uncertainty and give each case its own exact route (abstract).
coauthors: Judith Brugman, Dick den Hertog, Johan S. H. van Leeuwaarden

quotes.text: All three cases are handled by first reformulating the DRO problem as a robust problem and then applying advanced techniques from robust optimization.
By solving these problems to optimality, our framework can offer valuable insights into the conservatism and behavior of existing approximation-based DRO models.

title: Fast and Scalable Inference of Dynamical Systems via Integral Matching
contribution: Integral matching for identifying the parameters of nonlinear ODEs without ODE solvers or derivative estimates, batched for parallel gradients; three orders of magnitude faster than adjoint methods on chaotic systems (abstract).

quotes.text: Nonetheless, the inevitable statistical biases in flawed causal inferences may in fact be irrelevant in as much as they may have limited impact on the downstream optimization error in any resulting decision.

title: LIDS Publication# 2659 Robust linear optimization and coherent risk measures
contribution: LIDS-report version of S024: uncertainty sets for robust linear optimization constructed from coherent risk measures through their duality theorem (polyhedral and norm-bounded cases), with the converse correspondence (abstract).
